sources.entry: OctoBot - Cryptocurrency trading bot. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: OctoBot is a free, open-source Python crypto trading bot with a visual web interface that automates strategies such as grids, DCA, crypto baskets, and TradingView or AI-driven trading across many exchanges.
summary.what_it_does: OctoBot runs automated crypto trading strategies, including built-in grid, DCA, and crypto basket strategies, plus connectors for TradingView alerts and OpenAI or Ollama models. It includes technical analysis indicators (RSI, Moving Averages, MACD) and social indicators such as Google Trends and Reddit data. It connects to 15+ exchanges, including Binance, Coinbase, Bybit, Hyperliquid, MEXC and Kucoin, largely via the CCXT library. A manual OctoBot instance offers a built-in web interface, backtesting on historical data, paper trading, and optional Telegram control. The README also describes a newer beta "node mode" with a separate interface and mobile app for managing multiple automations from one dashboard.
use_cases: dollar cost averaging into crypto on a schedule
run a TradingView alert-based trading bot
backtest a crypto trading strategy on historical data
paper trade crypto before using real funds
control a trading bot through Telegram
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the OctoBot executable for Windows, MacOS, Linux or Raspberry Pi from the releases page
Or install from Python following the project's Python installation guide
notable: Built-in backtesting engine using historical exchange data (manual OctoBot only)
Supports AI trading through OpenAI models and local Ollama models
Can run as a self-custody node where keys stay on the user's devices (beta)
Minimum hardware of 1 core, 250 MB RAM and 1 GB disk
Runs on desktop, server, Raspberry Pi or cloud, with executables and a Docker image
caveats: The new node-mode interface is a beta and the README warns of bugs and incomplete features
Backtesting is only available in manual OctoBot instances, not in node mode
Some features, such as Bybit trading, are limited by upstream exchange API changes
The README includes a disclaimer that trading involves risk of losing money and the authors take no responsibility for results
keywords: run trading bot on raspberry pi
